programs.name: North Dakota Adults and Aging Services (State Unit on Aging)
programs.federal_name: Older Americans Act Title III-B / III-E (Area Agencies on Aging)
programs.about: North Dakota's state unit on aging funds local Area Agencies on Aging. Your local Area Agency on Aging may help with a home safety check or small changes; find it through the Eldercare Locator.

programs.name: North Dakota Assistive Technology Program
programs.about: North Dakota's federally funded assistive technology program; some AT programs help with home changes or link people to low-cost loans.

programs.name: North Dakota Centers for Independent Living
programs.about: Independent living centers in North Dakota give advice, skills training and referrals to people with disabilities; some help pay for home changes.

programs.name: VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH), Special Housing Adaptation (SHA), Temporary Residence Adaptation (TRA) and HISA grants
programs.federal_name: VA SAH / SHA / TRA / HISA grants

programs.name: North Dakota Division of Vocational Rehabilitation
programs.about: North Dakota Division of Vocational Rehabilitation may pay for home changes or devices when they help a person with a disability reach a job goal.

programs.name: Insurance: Health (e.g., Medicare) and HMOs, Long-Term Care, Life
programs.federal_name: Medicare / Medicare Advantage and private insurance

programs.name: North Dakota Medicaid
programs.about: North Dakota Medicaid runs North Dakota's Medicaid home and community-based waivers. Some waivers pay for home changes (often called environmental modifications) so a person with low income who needs long-term care can stay home. The USC ND state profile summarizes which waivers cover this.

programs.name: North Dakota Money Follows the Person Program
programs.about: Helps people with disabilities or chronic conditions move from a nursing home or other institution back to a home in the community. Services differ by state.

programs.name: Social Security: Plan for Achieving Self-Support (PASS) and Impairment-Related Work Expenses (IRWE)
programs.about: Work rules for people on SSI or SSDI. They can set money aside or subtract disability-related work costs, which may include home changes, so their benefits drop less.

programs.name: Community Development Block Grants (CDBG): State CDBG Program and CDBG Entitlement Program
HOME Program (local HOME grantees)
Local Housing/Neighborhood Agencies (Neighborhood Housing Services)
programs.about: Local nonprofit housing groups, such as NeighborWorks affiliates, may give repair advice, loans or grants. Search the NeighborWorks directory or your city name plus "Neighborhood Housing Services" to find groups in North Dakota.

programs.name: North Dakota Housing Finance Agency
programs.about: North Dakota Housing Finance Agency is North Dakota's housing finance agency. HFAs mostly fund home buying and affordable housing, and some offer low-interest or deferred repair loans. Check its site for any current repair or accessibility program.

programs.name: North Dakota USDA Rural Development offices (Bismarck, Devils Lake, Dickinson, Minot and Valley City area offices)
programs.federal_name: USDA Section 504 Home Repair loans and grants; Section 533 Housing Preservation Grants
programs.about: Rural North Dakota homeowners with very low income can ask these area offices about 504 repair loans and grants.

programs.name: North Dakota Weatherization Assistance Program
programs.about: Lowers energy bills for lower-income North Dakota households and can include small health and safety repairs.

programs.name: FHA Loan Insurance: Title I Home Improvement and 203(k) Purchase/Rehabilitation
Home Equity Line of Credit
programs.about: A credit line borrowed against the home's value that can be drawn on as needed for home changes. It is repaid with interest. Ask a local bank or credit union.

programs.name: Home Equity Loan
programs.about: A second mortgage that pays out a lump sum for home changes and is repaid on top of the first mortgage. Ask a local bank.

programs.name: Lender Unsecured/Personal Loans
programs.about: A personal loan from a bank puts no lien on the home, so it can work for renters and smaller projects. Approval depends on income, debt and credit.

programs.name: Mortgage Refinancing
programs.about: Replacing the current mortgage with a new one can free up cash for home changes when the owner has enough equity.

programs.name: Remodeler Donated Financing
programs.about: Some remodelers donate part of the labor, materials or financing for a project. Ask your contractor.

programs.name: Remodeler Referred Financing
programs.about: Many contractors partner with finance companies that lend for remodeling jobs. Ask your contractor what they offer.

programs.name: Reverse Equity Mortgage (FHA-approved Home Equity Conversion Mortgage)
Secured Loans Against Homeowner's Bank Accounts
programs.about: A bank may lend against a certificate of deposit the owner already holds. This can cover smaller projects.

programs.name: Secured Loans Against Homeowner's Financial Investment Accounts (Margin Loan)
programs.about: Some banks and brokerages let owners borrow against an investment account and use the money for home changes. Ask about the terms and risks first.

programs.name: Civic, Advocacy, Religious, and Trade Groups
programs.about: Churches, service clubs, trade unions and builder groups sometimes run volunteer projects such as ramp builds, or raise money for home changes. Call 211 to find groups in North Dakota.

programs.name: North Dakota Victims Services
programs.federal_name: Crime Victims' Benefits (U.S. Department of Justice)
programs.about: North Dakota's crime victim compensation may help pay for home accessibility changes after an injury from a crime, when insurance or restitution does not cover it.

programs.name: Social Security Title XX Social Services (Social Services Block Grant)
programs.about: State human services offices use these federal funds for emergencies. For people already on public assistance, they can sometimes cover a ramp, rails or grab bars.

programs.name: North Dakota Workforce Safety and Insurance
programs.about: If a work injury makes daily life at home hard, North Dakota workers' comp may pay for home changes or a move to a more suitable home.

programs.name: Internal Revenue Service: Personal Income Tax Deduction, Capital Gains Tax, Business Tax Deduction
State/Local Taxes: Sales Tax Exemption and Property Tax Exemption
programs.about: The lead list names no specific North Dakota credit. It notes that some states and counties exempt sales tax on accessibility items, and that home changes can raise assessed value. Check with the North Dakota revenue department and your county assessor.

notes: Standard USC template; no state-specific home modification grant or accessibility tax credit listed. MFP link is an older brochure PDF.
